about: Short reasons for known competitor behaviour. An entry explains a competitor cell that is differs or rejects when the cell's library and task are listed and the cell's first difference (detail) matches the pattern; the first matching entry is used. A reason describes what the library does, never a fault of the harness. An entry that matches nothing in a full run is stale and the report tool says so.

entries.reason: Writes a float with no fractional part (812.0) as 812, so a YAML 1.2 reader reads it back as an integer.
Reads through JSON, where every number is a float, so an integer comes back as a float.

entries.detail: got a mapping of \d+, expected a sequence of \d+
entries.reason: Reads one document of a multi-document stream, so the stream does not come back whole.
A YAML 1.1 reader: the plain scalar y is the boolean true.
A YAML 1.1 reader: the key on is the boolean true, so /on is not found.
Reads the document through sigs.k8s.io/yaml, a YAML 1.1 reader: the key on is the boolean true, so a path under /on is not found.
Writes a string that looks like a number (05509, 1.5) without quotes, so it reads back as a number.
A string that ends with a newline reads back without that final newline.
Writes the null spelled ~ as null.
Writes the escapes of a double-quoted scalar (\u00e9) as the characters themselves.
Does not keep the block literal style of the edited value: the new text is written as a plain scalar.
The yaml.Node tree keeps comments but not blank lines, spacing or a leading --- marker, and it lays flow collections out its own way, so the text it writes back is not the input.
Patches through the yaml.v3 node tree, which keeps comments but not blank lines, spacing or a leading --- marker, so the text it writes back differs from the input.
Patches through the goccy AST, which prints its own spacing and changes blank lines, so the text it writes back differs from the input.
The AST prints its own spacing for flow collections and trailing comments, and blank lines, quoting or a leading --- marker change, so the text it writes back is not the input.
Patches a JSON tree and writes it back as YAML, so comments, blank lines and quoting are not kept (it is not lossless).
Stops at its default nesting limit, which the benchmark leaves as it is.
Writes the edited value without the line break that follows it, joining it to the next line.
